# google_document_ai_schema_version

SchemaVersion is a version of the Schema which is created in Schema.


To get more information about SchemaVersion, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/document-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.schemas.schemaVersions)

## Example Usage - Documentai Schema Version


```hcl
resource "google_document_ai_schema" "schema" {
  location     = "us"
  display_name = "my-schema"
  labels = {
    "env" = "test"
  }
}

resource "google_document_ai_schema_version" "schema_version" {
  location     = "us"
  schema_id    = google_document_ai_schema.schema.name
  display_name = "my-schema-version"
  labels = {
    "env" = "test"
  }
  schema {
    display_name    = "test-doc-schema"
    description     = "Schema description"
    document_prompt = "Document prompt text"
    metadata {
      document_splitter              = true
      document_allow_multiple_labels = true
      prefixed_naming_on_properties  = false
      skip_naming_validation         = true
    }
    entity_types {
      name         = "document"
      display_name = "Document Root"
      base_types   = ["document"]
      properties {
        name            = "invoice_id"
        display_name    = "Invoice ID"
        value_type      = "invoice_id"
        occurrence_type = "OPTIONAL_ONCE"
        method          = "EXTRACT"
      }
      properties {
        name            = "payment_type"
        display_name    = "Payment Type"
        value_type      = "payment_type"
        occurrence_type = "OPTIONAL_MULTIPLE"
        method          = "DERIVE"
      }
    }
    entity_types {
      name         = "invoice_id"
      display_name = "Invoice ID"
      base_types   = ["string"]
    }
    entity_types {
      name         = "payment_type"
      display_name = "Payment Type"
      base_types   = ["string"]
      enum_values {
        values = ["CREDIT_CARD", "DEBIT_CARD", "WIRE"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The user-defined name of the SchemaVersion.

* `schema` -
  (Required)
  The schema of the SchemaVersion.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema).

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the resource.

* `schema_id` -
  (Required)
  The schema id that this schema version belongs to.


* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  The Google Cloud labels for the SchemaVersion.

  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_schema"></a>The `schema` block supports:

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  Display name to show users.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  Description of the schema.

* `document_prompt` -
  (Optional)
  Document-level prompt provided by the user. This custom text is injected into the AI model's prompt to provide extra, document-wide guidance for processing.

* `metadata` -
  (Optional)
  Metadata of the schema.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema_metadata).

* `entity_types` -
  (Optional)
  Entity types of the schema.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema_entity_types).


<a name="nested_schema_metadata"></a>The `metadata` block supports:

* `document_splitter` -
  (Optional)
  If true, a `document` entity type can be applied to subdocument (splitting). Otherwise, it can only be applied to the entire document (classification).

* `document_allow_multiple_labels` -
  (Optional)
  If true, on a given page, there can be multiple `document` annotations covering it.

* `prefixed_naming_on_properties` -
  (Optional)
  If set, all the nested entities must be prefixed with the parents.

* `skip_naming_validation` -
  (Optional)
  If set, this will skip the naming format validation in the schema. So the string values in `DocumentSchema.EntityType.name` and `DocumentSchema.EntityType.Property.name` will not be checked.

<a name="nested_schema_entity_types"></a>The `entity_types` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  Name of the type. It must be unique within the schema file and cannot be a "Common Type".

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  User defined name for the type.

* `base_types` -
  (Optional)
  The entity type that this type is derived from. For now, one and only one should be set.

* `enum_values` -
  (Optional)
  Defines a list of enum values.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema_entity_types_enum_values).

* `properties` -
  (Optional)
  Defines properties that can be part of the entity type.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_schema_entity_types_properties).


<a name="nested_schema_entity_types_enum_values"></a>The `enum_values` block supports:

* `values` -
  (Optional)
  The individual values that this enum values type can include.

<a name="nested_schema_entity_types_properties"></a>The `properties` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  The name of the property. Follows the same guidelines as the EntityType name.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  User defined name for the property.

* `value_type` -
  (Required)
  A reference to the value type of the property. This type is subject to the same conventions as the `Entity.base_types` field.

* `occurrence_type` -
  (Optional)
  Occurrence type limits the number of instances an entity type appears in the document.
  Possible values are: `OPTIONAL_ONCE`, `OPTIONAL_MULTIPLE`, `REQUIRED_ONCE`, `REQUIRED_MULTIPLE`.

* `method` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies how the entity's value is obtained.
  Possible values are: `EXTRACT`, `DERIVE`, `RELAXED_EXTRACT`.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/schemas/{{schema_id}}/schemaVersions/{{name}}`

* `name` -
  The resource name of the SchemaVersion.

* `create_time` -
  The time when the SchemaVersion was created.

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


SchemaVersion can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/schemas/{{schema_id}}/schemaVersions/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{schema_id}}/{{name}}`
* `{{location}}/{{schema_id}}/{{name}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import SchemaVersion using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    name = "<-optional value->"
    location = "<-required value->"
    schema_id = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_document_ai_schema_version.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import SchemaVersion using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/schemas/{{schema_id}}/schemaVersions/{{name}}"
  to = google_document_ai_schema_version.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), SchemaVersion can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_document_ai_schema_version.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/schemas/{{schema_id}}/schemaVersions/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_document_ai_schema_version.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{schema_id}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_document_ai_schema_version.default {{location}}/{{schema_id}}/{{name}}
```
